question.problem:
Consider the affine transformation $T,$ defined as

$$
x=2u-2v-3,\,y=u-v+2.
$$

What is the area scale factor of the transformation?
question.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that the given transformation can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2u-2v-3 \\ u-v+2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2u-2v \\ u-v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the matrix representation of the linear transformation associated with $T$ is $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}].$

Computing the determinant of $A,$ we get

$$
det(A)=|\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|=2\cdot (-1)-1\cdot (-2)=0.
$$

So, the area scale factor of the transformation is

$$
|det(A)|=|0|=0.
$$
